landing.metaTitle: LiftPilot — geared lift machine check for replacements
landing.metaDescription: Traction, rope, motor, brake and shaft checks for replacing a geared lift machine, with an automatic proposal and a PDF calculation report.
landing.h1: LiftPilot: choosing and checking the geared machine for a replacement
landing.answer: LiftPilot checks whether a geared machine suits the existing lift — traction in the three conditions of UNI EN 81-50, ropes, motor, brake, manual rescue and shaft — or proposes one, and prepares the calculation report (relazione di calcolo) for the technical file.
landing.status: In validation: an engineer is checking the normative values. Results stay indicative until the verification checklist is signed.
landing.feature1Text: Traction at loading, in emergency braking (8 cases, also at the brake’s real deceleration) and with the car stalled; ropes, D/d and safety factor; power and torque; brake; manual rescue; shaft and anchor loads.
landing.feature2Text: When no machine has been chosen yet, LiftPilot proposes sheave, groove, ratio, IEC motor and brake setting. In a replacement it keeps the number and diameter of the existing ropes.
landing.feature3Text: From every saved calculation, a report in Italian with the data, the checks, the clauses and the status of every normative value, ready to be checked and signed.
landing.feature4Text: Every calculation is an immutable snapshot with engine version, normative profile and SHA-256 fingerprint: the same data always give the same result.
landing.step1Text: Rated load, car mass, balance, speed, travel, machine layout (top, with a deflector or bottom) and geometry.
landing.step2Text: The nameplate data of the offered machine or the software’s proposal, compared with the existing machine.
landing.step3Text: Result in brief with a traffic light per area, complete technical tables and a PDF calculation report from the saved calculation.
landing.normsTitle: Which standards is it based on?
landing.normsLead: The software’s Italian normative profile includes:
landing.normsNote: Profile {profile}. Every value the software uses is tied to a document and clause in the standards registry; values from secondary sources are marked ⚠ until they are checked against the current text.
landing.faq1q: Does LiftPilot replace the report signed by the technician?
landing.faq1a: No. LiftPilot prepares the calculations and the report; the document becomes a calculation report when a qualified technician checks and signs it, and the responsibility stays with them.
landing.faq2q: Does it work with the machine at the bottom?
landing.faq2a: Yes. The calculation follows the rope path for a top machine with direct pull, a top machine with a deflector and a bottom machine with two pulleys at the top, including the upward load on the shaft.
landing.faq3q: Can I keep the existing ropes in a replacement?
landing.faq3a: Yes, that is the default: the new ropes have the same number and diameter as the installed ones, and the proposal keeps them too.
landing.faq4a: On servers in the European Union. A company’s projects are visible only to the users of that company.
landing.faq5a: The interface is in Italian, English and Bulgarian; the calculation report is in Italian.
landing.machineAlt: Geared machine on its bedplate: motor with cooling fins, drum brake with electromagnet, worm gearbox, handwheel for emergency operation and traction sheave with four ropes.
landing.machineCaption: The machine of the calculator’s example A: sheave D 560 mm, 4 ropes Ø 10 mm, ratio 1:43, 7.5 kW motor. Illustrative model, not a real product.

lift.about_loading: Car at the floor of the check, brake closed: people get in up to 1.25 times the rated load. The ropes must hold.
lift.about_stall: The counterweight rests on its buffers and the machine keeps turning upwards: the ropes must slip.
lift.sum_ride: From {from} to {to} with {load} kg: T1/T2 reaches at most {util} of the braking traction limit; motor torque up to {torque} N·m.
lift.sum_ride_over: From {from} to {to} with {load} kg: during the ride T1/T2 exceeds the braking traction limit ({util}); with the conventional friction the ropes would slip. Reduce the design acceleration or increase the traction (groove, wrap angle). Motor torque up to {torque} N·m.
lift.sum_brake_ok: The brake decelerates the car at {a} m/s²: T1/T2 reaches {util} of the limit and the ropes hold. Stop in {d0} cm.
lift.sum_brake_slip: The brake decelerates at {a} m/s²: T1/T2 asks {util} times the traction available and the ropes slip on the sheave. The car stops in {d1} cm instead of {d0} cm.
lift.sum_brake_runaway: The brake decelerates at {a} m/s², but T1/T2 passes the traction even with the car at rest: the ropes slip and the car runs on to the buffers.
lift.sum_brake_none: The brake does not stop the car: its torque ({tb} N·m) cannot hold it and the car runs on to the buffers.
lift.sum_brake_min: On its own the brake would decelerate at {a0} m/s²: the check uses the standard's minimum, {a} m/s².
lift.sum_loading_ok: With 1.25 times the rated load T1/T2 reaches {util} of the limit: the ropes hold and the car stays at the floor.
lift.sum_loading_fail: While loading T1/T2 passes the limit ({util}): the ropes slip and the car sinks with the doors open.
lift.sum_stall_ok: With the counterweight on its buffers T1/T2 reaches {efa} ({ratio}): the ropes slip and the car is not lifted.
lift.sum_stall_fail: With the counterweight on its buffers T1/T2 stays at {ratio} against {efa}: the ropes do not slip and the car is lifted toward the ceiling.
lift.sum_buffer_ok: Impact at 1.15 times the rated speed: the buffer compresses by {x} mm of {stroke} mm; peak deceleration {g} g.
lift.sum_buffer_fail: Impact at 1.15 times the rated speed: the stroke of {stroke} mm is not enough and the buffer goes solid.

legal.title: Privacy and terms of use
legal.metaDescription: How LiftPilot processes the personal data of installers and technicians, and the terms of use of the service.
legal.controllerText: Carbon Stealth VCC, Company ID BG208725180, ul. Samuil 3, 2670 Bobov Dol, Bulgaria. For privacy questions and to exercise your rights, write to info@carbonstealth.eu.
legal.dataTitle: What data do we process, and why?
legal.dataText:
Account: name, e-mail, company name, VAT number and city (if you enter them), password (only as an Argon2id hash), language, date of the last sign-in, confirmation of the address and acceptance of these terms (date and version). They are needed to provide the service (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, contract).

Activity log: who in your company did what and when (sign-ins, saved calculations, issued drawings), for security and for the traceability of technical documents (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interest).

Service e-mails: the confirmation of the address and the links for a new password, sent only when you register or ask for them.

Security: the IP address is used, in memory only, to limit repeated attempts and the application does not store it; the web server’s technical logs (IP, page, time) are kept for a limited time for security (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
legal.projectsTitle: And the data of the installations?
legal.projectsText: The installations, calculations and drawings your company enters may contain personal data, for example a client’s name or an installation’s address. We process them on your company’s behalf and only to provide the service (Art. 28 GDPR), never for other purposes.
legal.recipientsText: The server is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany), in the European Union; the service e-mails go through Brevo (France). Nobody else: we do not sell data and use no advertising or tracking tools.
legal.cookiesText: Technical cookies only: an httpOnly one for the session after sign-in (12 hours at most) and a session cookie (NEXT_LOCALE) that remembers the chosen language when it differs from the browser’s. No analytics, advertising or profiling cookies, which is why no consent banner is needed.
legal.retentionTitle: How long do we keep them?
legal.retentionText: The account and its data as long as the account exists; an account that is never confirmed or used (a registration, or a user added by a company) is deleted after {days} days. The activity log stays as long as the company’s account exists. You can ask for deletion at any time at info@carbonstealth.eu.
legal.rightsText: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection (Arts. 15–21 GDPR): write to info@carbonstealth.eu. You can lodge a complaint with the Bulgarian data protection authority (www.cpdp.bg) or with the authority of your country, in Italy the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (www.garanteprivacy.it). We take no automated decisions about you (Art. 22 GDPR).
legal.serviceText: LiftPilot is software by Carbon Stealth VCC for lift installers and technicians, for professional use: geared machine check, shaft design, simulation and drawings. It is in validation: an engineer is checking the normative values and the service may change.
legal.resultsTitle: Who is responsible for the results?
legal.resultsText: LiftPilot’s calculations, drawings and reports are drafts: they become documents only when a qualified technician checks and signs them, and the responsibility for the design stays with that technician. LiftPilot replaces neither the standards nor the technician’s judgement.
legal.accountsText: Whoever registers the company is its owner: they add colleagues, choose their roles and answer for the accounts of their company. Everyone keeps their own password secret. We may suspend an account in case of abuse or a security risk.
legal.lawText: Bulgarian law; the Bulgarian courts have jurisdiction. Questions: info@carbonstealth.eu.
